title: molt new-user --from <dir>: scaffold a user stack from a template other than Molt's skeleton, by the same code and tokens
body:
`molt new-user` scaffolds a user stack only from Molt's own skeleton, `templates/molt-user`, a fixed path in `molt_new_user` (`lib/newuser.sh`) with no option for another template. hv's bootcamp gives each participant their own `Molt-<login>`, scaffolded at first run from a course template in the image (hv's ruling, 5 Nov, through pipeliner-sc). That template cannot go through new-user today, so a first-run script would need a second scaffolder of its own, which could drift from Molt's.

hv chose option (a) of molt-vc's answer to pipeliner-sc (`/Users/matts/Devel/scratch/molt-vc/answer-pipeliner-sc-2026-11-05.md`, its addendum), and allocated it in molt-vc's window on 5 Nov.

The change:
- `--from <dir>` names the template new-user scaffolds from. Without it, new-user uses Molt's own skeleton, as now.
- The template goes through the same code: the same `__MOLT_*__` tokens are substituted in file contents and path names, so Molt keeps one scaffolder. No `.git` directory is copied from the template.
- new-user refuses a `--from` that is not a directory, or that holds no `config/`, since a stack is found by its `config/`. Each refusal names the path and why, and nothing is written.
- Every value can come from flags, so a first-run script never meets a prompt.
- The next steps new-user prints keep the resleeve, `git init` and the first commit for any template. The GitHub remote lines stay for Molt's own skeleton only.

Size S.

## As built

Merged at 4116a1b, from d3cbb75 on `dc/doctor-participant`, with 66a291f and cd73db0 from vc's review.

- `--from <dir>` names the template. Without it, new-user uses Molt's skeleton, as before. `molt_new_user` takes the template as its seventh argument.
- One copy function, `_molt_copy_template`, serves the skeleton and `--from` alike. It takes no `.git` at any depth, file or directory.
- One list of the five tokens serves file contents and path names. It is `_molt_subst_text`, a sed from stdin to stdout, with each value escaped. Path names are renamed deepest first, each entry by its own name, so a tokened entry inside a tokened directory lands where it should.
- vc's review brought three fixes, each with its own test:
  - An `&` in a value stays whole in a path name under bash 5.2 and later. Before, `${name//token/value}` put the token back in the `&`'s place, through patsub_replacement.
  - Each file keeps its mode, since the result is written back into the file, so a template's scripts stay executable.
  - Both seds run under `LC_ALL=C`, so on macOS, under a UTF-8 locale, a file that is not UTF-8, such as an image, arrives byte for byte. That test cannot be red on Linux, where GNU sed passes such a file either way.
- A `--from` that is not a directory, an empty one included, or that holds no `config/`, is refused, naming the path and why, with nothing written.
- The next steps keep the resleeve, `git init` and the first commit. The GitHub lines are the skeleton's alone.
- `molt help`, `docs/guides/new-user.md` and the CHANGELOG name it.
- The tests are in `test/newuser.bats`, each red at its base and green at its fix under both bashes. The file passed whole at the final head, 25 of 25 under each.

Owed:
- pipeliner-dc's run of the course template through `molt new-user --from` on 1.4.5 from brew, which closes AE ST0002/07; molt-vc tells it when brew has 1.4.5 (vc todo 47);
- the full suite and CI, at hv's 1.4.5 cut.

Met, 5 Nov 2026: in agentic-engineering-dc's AE ST0002/07 run (slot 01M6NTEV9BP73YR1WC5PJFQGXM, 12:22Z to 12:25Z on 5 Nov 2026), in the bootcamp's amd64 image on brew's Molt 1.4.5 (39fa08efb062), `molt new-user tester --from /usr/local/share/devvm/molt-template`, with every value given as a flag and `--dest ~/cfg/Molt-tester`, then `molt resleeve`, ended "Sleeve ready", and `molt status` named the sleeve devvm and the stack ~/cfg/Molt-tester. No `__MOLT_` token was left in the stack. After `git init` and the first commit, its git status was clean, and `git config user.email` and the new key's comment were both the person's email. The full suite and CI passed at the 1.4.5 cut (release commit 39fa08e: candidate run 42020687220, main run 42023418293).
